sections.h2: Does Northampton Township require an inspection when a house sells?
sections.html:
No. The township's building and zoning FAQ says Northampton does not conduct an inspection or require a certificate for the resale of residential property. That makes a Northampton sale simpler on the municipal side than in towns with a resale permit, though a certificate of use and occupancy is still required to occupy a nonresidential space.

Permits still apply to projects, including replacements. The township notes that an old shed or fence may never have been approved, so replacing it needs a permit and a fresh look at current rules. Sheds of 240 square feet or less generally go behind the house, seven feet from the property line and no taller than 12 feet. Fences go in side and rear yards at up to six feet, never in easements, and corner lots and pool fences have special requirements.

The administration building is at 55 Township Road in Richboro, and the main line is 215-357-6800.

sections.h2: What is Northampton Township's layout and housing history?
sections.html:
Northampton Township is a second class township of about 26 square miles in Bucks County, roughly 12 miles northeast of Philadelphia. It became a township on December 14, 1722, and the Neshaminy Creek forms its entire northeastern edge. Its communities include Churchville, Holland, Ivyland and Richboro, and the township says Jacksonville became Ivyland, Addisville became Richboro and Rocksville became Holland.

Farmland turned into subdivisions in the second half of the twentieth century. Wikipedia lists the population at 6,006 in 1960, 35,406 in 1990 and 39,915 in 2020, which suggests much of the housing dates from those decades.

Route 332 crosses the township along Jacksonville Road, Almshouse Road and Newtown Richboro Road, while Route 232 runs north and south along Second Street Pike, Route 532 follows Buck Road and Route 213 skirts the southeast border. The township maintains about 171 of its 202 miles of public roads. Students attend the Council Rock School District, and Tyler State Park offers 1,711 acres of trails.

sections.h2: Does private well water affect a Northampton sale?
sections.html:
It can, because groundwater contamination from the former Naval Air Warfare Center in Warminster has moved into Northampton Township. The township states that the Navy has identified affected private wells and committed to some remediation, but that it believes more is needed, and it urges owners with wells to test.

Northampton Bucks County Municipal Authority supplies public water to thousands of residents and businesses, and the township page links to an authority announcement of a public water connection project for 334 homes. A seller on a private well should expect questions from buyers and lenders. Practical steps include:

  • Test the well through a laboratory from the accredited list the township posts.
  • Ask the Municipal Authority at 215-357-8515 whether public water is available at the address.
  • Keep any Navy or authority correspondence about the property with the sale documents.

sections.h2: What do Northampton Township property taxes include?
sections.html:
The 2026 township real estate rate is 35.250 mills, built from eight separate levies. The township's tax page uses a $40,000 median assessed home in its example, which produces a $1,410 township bill at that rate.

2026 Northampton Township millage breakdown (source: township tax information page)

The elected tax collector bills real estate tax from an office on Bustleton Pike in Richboro and accepts no cash, with a separate check for each bill. Earned income tax runs 1 percent and splits evenly between the township and Council Rock School District, and the local services tax is $52 a year for people who work in the township.

sections.h2: How do Bucks County assessment appeals work for Northampton owners?
sections.html:
Bucks County's Board of Assessment Appeals takes annual appeals once a year in early August, and the 2026 deadline was August 3, 2026, with any change effective for the 2027 tax year. Residential appeal forms and rules are posted on the county site, a fee applies, and the board's office is at 55 East Court Street in Doylestown.

Homeowners can also file a Homestead/Farmstead Exclusion application, and the county sets March 1 as the deadline for the tax year beginning the following July 1. The board meets on the first and third Tuesday of each month at 10 a.m.

The county also notes that Act 29 requires a new owner to send contact information to the Board of Assessment within 30 days of purchase.

sections.h2: What transfer taxes and recording rules apply to a Northampton sale?
sections.html:
Bucks County states that a sale carries a 2 percent transfer tax, with 1 percent to the state and 1 percent to the municipality and school district, paid at recording. State and local law do not say who pays, and in most agreements the buyer and seller split it, though the new owner is responsible if the amount paid is questioned.

Since January 2026 the Recorder of Deeds no longer accepts personal checks for this tax. Accepted payment is cash in the office, a cashier's check, a money order or a credit card. Family transfers between spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, and siblings can be exempt, and a Statement of Value (REV-183) goes in duplicate whenever the true value is not on the deed or an exemption is claimed.

If the state later finds the property worth more than stated, additional tax and interest are billed directly by the Department of Revenue.

sections.h2: What should a Northampton seller know about utilities, trash and transit?
sections.html:
Public water and sewer questions go to the Northampton Bucks County Municipal Authority, and trash and recycling are handled by the township's contractor, J. P. Mascaro and Sons, at 800-432-1616. The township posts a street listing that shows each pickup day, which is useful to hand a buyer.

Commuters have limited rail choices. The TMA Bucks Richboro-Warminster Rushbus runs peak-hour shuttles from Richboro to the SEPTA Warminster station, and passenger service on the old Fox Chase-Newtown line through Churchville and Holland ended in January 1983, with the Holland station demolished in 2000.

The township's capital project list includes Holland streetscape improvements, a Jacksonville and Almshouse Road roundabout, the Richboro sidewalk project and a Route 332 trail connection, all of which buyers may see while driving through.

sections.h2: Who buys homes in Northampton Township, and when is a cash sale useful?
sections.html:
Northampton is a high-value, stable market: QuickFacts shows $599,100 for a typical owned home, 93.8 percent of units occupied by their owners, and median household income of $158,583, with 95.4 percent of residents at the same address as the prior year. Seniors make up 22.2 percent of the population, and the average commute runs 30.5 minutes.

A cash sale becomes useful when a house needs work the owner cannot fund or when timing is tight. Situations that often lead there include:

  • An estate property with an older kitchen, roof or heating system.
  • A house with a private well that failed a test.
  • An owner relocating before a listing could reasonably sell.

Weigh the cash number against a listing's net after commissions, repairs and the 2 percent transfer tax.

faqs.q: Do I need a use and occupancy certificate to sell my Northampton house?
faqs.a: No. The township says it does not inspect or require a certificate for the resale of residential property. A certificate of use and occupancy applies to nonresidential space.

faqs.q: What is the Northampton Township real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The 2026 township millage is 35.250 mills, made up of general purpose, fire, emergency medical, recreation, debt service, library and two road levies. County and Council Rock School District taxes are billed on top of that.

faqs.q: When was the Bucks County appeal deadline in 2026?
faqs.a: The deadline for 2026 annual appeals was August 3, 2026, and any change takes effect for the 2027 tax year. Annual appeals are due in early August each year.

faqs.q: How much is the realty transfer tax in Bucks County?
faqs.a: Bucks County lists it at 2 percent, with 1 percent to the state and 1 percent to the municipality and school district. It is paid at recording, and the buyer and seller usually split it.

faqs.q: Should I test a private well before selling in Northampton Township?
faqs.a: Yes, testing is a sensible step, because the township reports groundwater contamination from the former Naval Air Warfare Center in Warminster. Use a laboratory from the accredited list the township posts and ask the Municipal Authority about public water.
